question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: Explicit repeat request after a model switch: adversarially review the Markdown audit as a last pass and find anything omitted.
requirements: Reconcile the current review, settled persisted-identity law and later conversion execution before changing the target.
Census every named platejs/markdown export, core Markdown authoring type, public policy field, material production call shape and legacy/helper unit.
Preserve representable syntax, references, exact source diagnostics and serialized persisted identity; diagnose unsupported loss.
Keep feature ownership and exact editor inference while deleting public or internal machinery with no independent current job.
Challenge the strongest deletion or replacement, including public options, detached helpers, extension wrappers and compiled dispatch.
Assessment and review-history repair only; no product implementation or downstream plan.
evidenceReuse: Reused the current source-matching audit's parser, mapping and serializer probes plus focused existing-test receipts. Rechecked current public barrels, policy types, production consumers, compiled mapping/runtime owners, package optional dependencies, identity doctrine and the August/September adoption plans. Two bounded independent source reviews challenged behavior claims and the public/helper census. Added a five-assertion disposable counterexample for MDX filter identity and mention whitespace; no broad suite was replayed.
summary: Pursue the Markdown redesign, but supersede the initial audit in material ways. Retain serialized persisted identity and compatible reads; replace only its broken alternate list path. Cut public node filters, public withoutMdx, the eager remarkMdx wrapper, line-oriented splitLineBreaks, detached parseMarkdownSlice/parseMarkdownInline and dead processor/stripping helpers. Move mention syntax into feature ownership, compile one source/tag/model/mark dispatch instead of modern mappings plus legacy rules, and make editor serialize input exact. Preserve parse/serialize naming, editor document/slice/inline jobs, detached document parse/serialize, broad standalone Value, feature-owned mappings and the platejs/markdown package. The current one-encoder model cannot report another feature's omitted properties, so Task must design the smallest composable property contribution/accounting hook or explicitly narrow the fidelity promise. All 31 Markdown-subpath exports, seven core authoring types, 15 unique policy fields, 17 production call shapes and 18 helper/legacy units were dispositioned across ten Pursue units.

alternatives: Retain the initial audit unchanged: Stop; its persisted-ID cut contradicts settled data law and its 10/10 count did not census the public API.
Repair allowedNodes, disallowedNodes and allowNode: Stop; no production consumer pays for a selector family that overlaps schema selection and mixes source kinds, tags, marks and model properties.
Keep Plate remarkMdx plus public withoutMdx: Stop; they create an eager optional dependency and hidden function-identity protocol around one extension.
Keep mention syntax in generic Markdown: Stop; the feature owns the dialect and can contribute parser behavior without a public generic MentionNode.
Keep modern decodeBySource plus legacy rules: Stop; duplicate dispatch causes selector mismatch and prevents composable property ownership.
Cut all standalone conversion or all fragment parsing: Stop; detached document conversion and installed editor fragment parsing are distinct current jobs.
Cut serialized block identity: Stop; it violates Plate's persisted-identity law and strands compatible serialized wrappers.
Introduce a universal codec or move Markdown into Plite: Stop; no substrate or cross-format job pays for another package or universal session.
Keep the Markdown package and naming, shrink unearned API, compile one dispatch, compose feature syntax/property contributions and use one durable-ID/list path: Pursue.
proofLimits: Read-only product audit; only review artifacts and ledger metadata changed. Current product source fingerprints match the initial audit. Existing focused runs and probes were reused rather than replayed. The new last-pass probe intentionally reports 0 pass and 5 fail for three MDX filter-identity defects plus newline/tab mention loss. A direct raw remark-mdx probe rejected the suspected exclusion bypass. Source inspection proves eager imports, caller absence, broad serialize input and duplicate maps; it does not prove the future contribution API, runtime cost or external consumer absence. No implementation, full typecheck/package suite, browser/native clipboard, external viewer, benchmark or arbitrary-property corpus ran.
